title: Judge temporarily stops border construction in Texas' Big Bend region
summary:
A federal judge has temporarily stopped border wall construction and related projects in Texas' Big Bend region. The decision includes Big Bend National Park, known for its landscapes, limestone cliffs and clear views of the night sky.

Judge Kathleen Cardone issued the ruling on Friday. It covers a border region about 500 miles long. The pause gives the court time to consider a lawsuit. It is not a final decision about whether the projects can go ahead.

An environmental organization, supporters of a historic church and a river guide brought the case. They argue that the Department of Homeland Security wrongly set aside rules protecting nature, cultural places and archaeological sites. Archaeology is the study of past people through objects and places they left behind.

The construction plans are part of the Trump administration's wider border project. Landowners, businesses and environmental groups have opposed work in Big Bend. Republicans and Democrats also objected after land clearing began inside the park in August.

The administration says it is reviewing plans for the national park. Federal agencies did not immediately answer requests for comment on Friday's ruling.

Park advocates welcomed the pause. They asked officials to repair damage already done and discuss other plans with local residents.
why_it_matters: The ruling affects construction in a national park and the surrounding region. The case concerns rules meant to protect nature and cultural places.
